message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most effective exercises you can do to build strength, size, and stability in your legs. I’ve grouped them by the primary muscle they target (quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves) and noted whether they’re body‑weight or weighted options so you can mix and match based on your equipment and goals.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles | Body‑Weight / Weighted | Key Tips |
|----------|-----------------|------------------------|----------|
| **Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings, core | Body‑weight, goblet, barbell, dumbbell | Keep chest up, knees tracking over toes, depth to parallel or below if mobility allows. |
| **Front Squat** | Quads, core, upper back | Barbell | Hands on bar, elbows high, keep torso upright. |
| **Back Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings, lower back | Barbell | Rack height, foot width shoulder‑wide, depth to parallel. |
| **Split Squat / Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Body‑weight, dumbbells, barbell | Back foot elevated on bench/box, knee stays above ankle. |
| **Lunge (forward, reverse, walking)** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Body‑weight, dumbbells, barbell | Step long enough to keep knee behind toes, maintain upright torso. |
| **Step‑Up** | Quads, glutes, calves | Body‑weight, dumbbells, barbell | Use a sturdy box or bench; drive through heel of stepping foot. |
| **Deadlift (Romanian, sumo, conventional)** | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back | Barbell, dumbbells | Keep back neutral, hinge at hips, pull through heels. |
| **Hip Thrust / Glute Bridge** | Glutes, hamstrings | Body‑weight, barbell, dumbbell | Squeeze glutes at top, avoid hyperextending lower back. |
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Machine | Adjust foot placement for quad vs glute emphasis. |
| **Hamstring Curl (lying or seated)** | Hamstrings | Machine, resistance band | Full range, slow eccentric phase. |
| **Calf Raise (standing, seated, single‑leg)** | Calves | Body‑weight, dumbbells, barbell | Full stretch at bottom, pause at peak contraction. |
| **Box Jump / Plyometric Jump** | Quads, glutes, calves, power | Body‑weight | Land softly, use arms for momentum, focus on explosive takeoff. |
| **Wall Sit** | Quads | Body‑weight | Hold for time, keep knees at 90°, chest up. |

### How to Structure a Leg‑Day Routine

1. **Warm‑up** – 5–10 min of light cardio (bike, row, jog) + dynamic stretches (leg swings, hip circles).  
2. **Compound Lift** – Start with a heavy compound movement (squat, deadlift, or leg press). 3–4 sets × 4–8 reps.  
3. **Accessory Movements** – Add 2–3 secondary lifts targeting different angles or smaller muscles. 3 sets × 8–15 reps.  
4. **Calf Work** – Finish with calf raises or plyometrics. 3 sets × 12–20 reps.  
5. **Cool‑down** – Light static stretching for quads, hamstrings, calves, glutes.  

### Sample 3‑Day Split

| Day | Focus | Example Sets/Reps |
|-----|-------|-------------------|
| **Leg Day 1** | Quads & Core | Back Squat 4×6, Walking Lunge 3×12, Leg Press 3×10, Plank 3×60 s |
| **Leg Day 2** | Hamstrings & Glutes | Romanian Deadlift 4×8, Bulgarian Split Squat 3×10, Hip Thrust 3×12, Calf Raise 3×15 |
| **Leg Day 3** | Power & Endurance | Front Squat 3×5, Box Jump 3×8, Seated Leg Curl 3×15, Wall Sit 3×90 s |

Feel free to swap out exercises or adjust rep ranges based on whether you’re focusing on hypertrophy (8–12 reps), strength (4–6 reps), or endurance (15+ reps). If you’re new to any movement, start with body‑weight or lighter loads to master form before adding weight. Happy training!
